items.title: Madkour: Is anything being overlooked?
items.summary: Abraham Madkour recounts a Clemson University sports marketing class where a student asked what challenges sports leaders are overlooking. His answer was whether the industry is meeting consumers' actual desire for sport in a bullish market full of new leagues, events and startups, warning against conflating investor desire with what the market wants. He also cautioned against pricing out the everyday fans who built the business, and noted the students' questions on premium experiences, private equity and global expansion.
items.what_it_means: With money pouring into new leagues and events, real fan demand is the test that matters, ahead of investor appetite.

items.title: NHL's next TV deal will test the league's strength
items.summary: The NHL can begin formal talks with ESPN and Skydance-owned TNT Sports on 1 January and is asking for a 50% to 100% increase over the seven-year, $4.5 billion deal it signed in 2021, according to sources who spoke to CNBC. The league can point to record playoff audiences averaging 1.8 million a game, a regular season up 25% and huge ratings for international hockey, while Skydance's priorities are paying down debt and funding a possible NFL increase of $1 billion a season or more. CNBC frames the outcome as the first public test of how media companies value sports rights outside the NFL.
items.what_it_means: The NHL's price will set a marker for what broadcasters and streamers pay for sport beyond the NFL, with MLB next to market.

items.title: PGA of America ready for Frisco closeup with 2027 PGA Championship
items.summary: The 2027 PGA Championship at PGA Frisco in Texas, the first men's major in the state since 1969, has sold all championship-round passes and all weeklong and daily hospitality inventory six months out. Championship director Jason Mengel said gross revenue will beat the 2026 record by 10% to 20%, and the hospitality build will pass 500,000 square feet, the largest in the event's history. The PGA of America says taking the championship to new markets that are excited to host it is part of how it grows the game.
items.what_it_means: Scarcity in a new market can sell out a major's premium inventory months before the event, freeing organisers to focus on the fan experience.

items.title: Modelo becomes NCAA's first-ever official beer in landmark partnership
items.summary: Constellation Brands' Modelo has become the first official beer of the NCAA, with exclusive beer-category rights across more than 90 men's and women's championships, including March Madness. Modelo will lift its college basketball investment by 65% year on year, run its first ad campaign built for the tournaments and activate through broadcast integrations on CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV, retail promotions and on-site experiences. Constellation's Mallika Monteiro said its sports investments start with what fans are passionate about and where they spend their time.
items.what_it_means: Newly opened alcohol categories give college sport a fresh sponsorship revenue line, and the first buyer has taken year-round access across the championship calendar.

items.title: Creator Sports Events Are Becoming Premium Branded Video
items.summary: Drawing on Tubefilter's weekly ranking of the most-watched branded YouTube videos, WeRSM notes the list is dominated by boxing, golf, football and creator-led entertainment. The Internet Invitational, a creator golf tournament whose first episode brought 64 golfers together for more than five hours, reached 12.1 million views with Reese's, DraftKings, Dunkin and ZYRTEC across the property, while DAZN and Lowe's backed other sports-led creator content. The piece argues brands are increasingly buying into creator formats that already behave like programming.
items.what_it_means: Creator-made sports events are becoming sponsorable media properties that compete with traditional sport for fan time and brand budgets.

items.title: MotoGP and ESPN Announce Two-Year Media Rights Agreement for U.S. and Latin America
items.summary: MotoGP has signed a two-year deal making ESPN its exclusive US media rights holder across linear networks for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, with races shown live or on same-day delay. In Latin America, ESPN continues coverage across 18 countries with streaming on Disney+, and rights for select events in Argentina and Brazil can be sublicensed to free-to-air broadcasters. MotoGP deputy CEO Carlos Ezpeleta framed the deal as a chance to introduce the sport to new audiences while serving existing fans.
items.what_it_means: Smaller global properties are using the reach of a major US broadcaster to find new fans in the Americas.

items.title: Yamaha Corporation to Acquire Disguise for Next Phase of Growth
items.summary: Yamaha Corporation has announced it will acquire Disguise, the visual technology company behind live experiences for tours by Beyoncé, Taylor Swift and Bad Bunny and venues including the Stade de France. Yamaha said people are seeking richer, more immersive live entertainment where audio, video, lighting and media come together across an entire space, and the deal combines its music heritage with Disguise's visual technology.
items.what_it_means: Major equipment makers are betting on immersive live production as audiences expect more from a night out.
